extracted.intended_audience: inventors, in-house counsel, patent attorneys and companies seeking to obtain patents in Brazil (foreign applicants included)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural criteria for obtaining and accelerating patent grants before the Brazilian INPI, including eligibility for priority/expedited tracks, PPH use, backlog-reduction mechanisms, and statutory patent-term rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term guarantee (Art. 40, LPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee’s monopoly is guaranteed for 20 years from the filing date or 10 years after the patent is granted, whichever is longer; Art. 40, LPI. Sole Paragraph: The term of validity shall not be less than ten (10) years for the patent and seven (7) years for the utility certificate from the date of grant, except in cases where the INPI is prevented from examining the merits of the application, due to a court case or in cases of force majeure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the patent is granted very late, the monopoly is guaranteed to last at least 10 years from the date of grant (and 7 years for utility certificates), so delayed grants can extend effective protection beyond the 20-year filing-term. Consider this when assessing portfolio value and prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for accelerated substantive examination — applicant categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request an accelerated substantive examination in the following cases: Depositors (individuals) over 60 years of age; Patent applications infringed by third parties; Applicants needing a granted patent to obtain financing for the commercial exploitation of their inventions; Depositors (natural persons) with physical or mental disabilities or serious illnesses; Patent applications for the treatment of AIDS, cancer, rare or neglected diseases; Patent applications filed by small companies; Applications from scientific and technological institutions; Applications filed in Brazil give priority to applications filed abroad; Patent applications covering green technologies; Patent applications filed by startups; and Patent applications covering technologies for the treatment of COVID-19 (pharmaceutical products and processes; healthcare equipment and/or materials for the diagnosis, prophylaxis and treatment of COVID-19).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant falls into any listed category, file a request for accelerated substantive examination under INPI Regulation no. 247/20 (priority examination procedures). Prepare supporting evidence (e.g., proof of age, company size, financing needs, medical condition, or link to prioritized technology) to accompany the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for accelerated substantive examination — third-party and public-interest requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons may request an accelerated substantive examination: Third parties accused of wrongfully copying the subject matter of a patent application; A third party who owns a technology that has subsequently been registered as a patent; The Ministry of Health, in the case of patent applications for medicines acquired by the National Public Health System (SUS); and The State when a national emergency is declared or when there is a public interest in examining a specific request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties and public authorities may trigger expedited handling; this can be used both offensively (to challenge or clear a path) and defensively (to obtain certainty). Prepare documentary proof of the claimed relationship (e.g., evidence of copying or ownership, official Ministry/State declarations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) pilot program for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: A new accelerated substantive examination procedure exists for applications subject to a PPH (Patent Prosecution Highway) pilot program. Since 01/12/2019 a PPH pilot program with standardized requirements and governed by a single regulation (n°252/19) is in force. The Brazilian INPI has signed PPH agreements with numerous patent offices (Japan, Argentina, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica, Denmark, El Salvador, Ecuador, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Europe-EPO, United States, United Kingdom, Dominican Republic, China, Austria, Sweden and South Korea).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims have been allowed/granted by a partner office, consider entering the PPH pilot program and file standardized PPH documentation per Reg. 252/19 to obtain accelerated substantive examination in Brazil. Ensure claims submitted in Brazil correspond to the allowed claims abroad and comply with the program's formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog reduction plan — objectives and target delivery times (Reg. 240/19 and 241/19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: To reduce the backlog by 80% by the end of 2021, and thereafter maintain an average delivery time of 2 to 3 years from the request for substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The INPI's public target influences expectations for examination timelines; applicants can plan prosecution and commercialization timing around a projected 2–3 year substantive examination window for applications covered by the plan. Monitor INPI announcements for updated performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog reduction plan — applications covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications concerned: All applications filed before 12/31/2016, and for which the results of the prior art search or examination are available in the context of corresponding patent application procedures of the same family conducted by a foreign office. These applications precisely cover around 80% of unexamined applications by the Brazilian INPI in August 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application predates 2017 and has a family member examined/searched abroad with available reports, it is likely covered by the backlog-reduction plan. Check the foreign family file numbers and make the correspondence clear in filings to trigger inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlog reduction plan — operational process and applicant recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan is based on the mass publication of standardized reports, essentially a list of prior art cited by a foreign office. Applicants are invited to submit the same claims accepted for a counterpart foreign patent and/or supporting arguments used abroad. The Brazilian INPI can also take advantage of the fact that no response to these reports needs to be filed in the event of an abandoned application. Abandoned applications can therefore be rejected without substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice given: 'file the same claims in Brazil as you would in any other country!' Submitting claims aligned with granted foreign claims and reusing supporting arguments used abroad will speed up grant under the plan. Also be aware that abandoned counterparts may lead to rejection without substantive examination, so monitor family prosecution status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory framework underpinning priority/examination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reforms and programs cited include: Law on Economic Freedom (Law no. 13.874/2019); Innovation Law (Law no. 13.243/2016) and Decree no. 9.283/2018; INPI Regulations no. 247/20 (priority examination procedures), no. 252/19 (PPH pilot), and no. 240/19 and 241/19 (backlog combat plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cited laws and INPI regulations as the legal basis when preparing requests for priority/accelerated examination or PPH filings. Referencing the correct regulation numbers and legal provisions in submissions will help ensure procedural compliance and smoother processing.
